newsitem.title: UK: Britain sets up human genetics commission.
newsitem.headline: Britain sets up human genetics commission.

text.p: The British government said on Monday it had set up a commission to advise on the sometimes emotive issue of human genetics, including gene therapy.

The Human Genetics Advisory Commission includes lawyers, scientists, doctors, journalists and will be headed by Sir Colin Campbell, Vice Chancellor of the University of Nottingham, Britain's Office of Science and Technology said in a statement.

"The advisory commission will be considering the broad social, ethical, and/or economic consequences of developments in human genetics, for example, in relation to public health, insurance, patents and employment," Science and Technology Minister Ian Taylor said in a statement.
The committee will advise government ministers from both the Office of Science and Technology and the health ministry. It will also report to the government's Chief Medical Officer.
"They will also advise on ways to build public confidence in the new science," Taylor said

Taylor said the committee would convene as soon as possible in 1997. "Human genetics...offers major opportunities for improving the quality of life and for wealth creation but also raises sensitive and complex issues which need to be addressed."
The group will aim to look ahead to potentially controversial developments and come up with ways to minimise public concerns.
Issues it is sure to discuss include prenatal genetic testing and whether tests can be required for a genetic predisposition to breast cancer.
